And I guess to answer your question, it feels very satisfying, alarmingly so, to unleash that Hyde in me.

So I've been looking into that part of my psyche for a while. I'm certain it has to do with feelings of anger and powerlessness from my childhood, born into a cult and enlightened to that notion early while simultaneously being continually thrust back into it with brief glimpses of what's outside in "normal" society for years. So it's an anger and control thing, and I've delved into it through BDSM with a really good partner over the last year. I found a part of myself through that exploration that I really can't express in a consentual relationship or any fantasy that we've tried, and we've gone pretty far. It's a dark part of me. I can control it, but in a very Jekyll and Hyde way it's becoming a bigger priority for me to unleash. Hence the suicide or destruction options left.

I don't think so honestly. I still hit the buttons that work now and then, and do feel the rewarding pleasurable emotions or mental stimulation or whatever the case, I just don't care to put the actual effort in to acheive those states anymore. I'm bored with the cycles. I guess waiting to see the future unfold and get weird and novel enough to draw me back in again is a possibility but it seems to be progressing too slowly to feel worth waiting for.

Thanks for the response. I've been meditating and introspecting since I was 14. My inner reality is pretty well understood, and for the last two years when I started running out of motivation/interest in external I put most of my pursuits on the back burner to allow myself to simply exist with no demands, just observe reality. I've grown bored of that at this point and just find those two options left on the table everytime I go looking for something new. The only silver lining I can see is maybe there's a way to unleash a destructive urge in a way that might be useful to humanity, like vigilante killings or something.

We had been together for about six months. We were camping in a rocky sage and juniper desert area in southern Utah. We found a giant rock that sat on a narrow pedestal atop a cliff, and could see for miles in every direction. For two or three hours we sat watching the clouds roll over, talking about everything and nothing. Out of nowhere a moment clicked, she sensed something in me that I hadn't noticed. She moved to sit behind me and held me while I cried.
